comparator.name: Humanistic Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official bachelor page, checked 2026-09-29, defines a three-year full-time Humanistic Studies programme of 60 ECTS per year and describes the current year-level content. Year one builds foundations in Humanistic Studies, psychology, philosophy, research and normative professionalisation; year two applies history, embodied meaning and citizenship to cases, critical reasoning and intervention design; year three combines a thesis, professional identity, research, guidance and advisory skills with specialization through electives, a minor or study abroad. The official 2025 accreditation report independently confirms the 180-EC degree, its meaning-making, humanisation, research and academic/professional-skills learning lines, and the curriculum revision expanding elective/minor space to 30 EC from 2026-2027. The current public page does not allocate every named activity to individual credits, so the comparator preserves the official 60+60+60 year structure and splits the final year into the documented 30-EC specialization space and the remaining 30-EC thesis/professional core without inventing course titles.
components: Year 1: Humanistic Studies foundations and orientation
Introduction to Humanistic Studies, psychology, philosophy, research, normative professionalisation and academic/personal development.
Year 2: interdisciplinary deepening and societal application
History, embodied meaning, citizenship, case-based work, critical reasoning, research and intervention design.
Independent bachelor research, professional identity, research ability, and guidance/advisory skills.
Year 3: specialization, minor or study abroad
Current 30-EC choice space introduced by the 2026-2027 curriculum revision; content depends on the student's approved selection.

alternatives.label: Humanistic studies, meaning & humane society
alternatives.concept: An interdisciplinary Humanistic Studies programme combining philosophy, sociology, psychology, history, research and public communication to examine meaning, values, flourishing and a humane society.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum balances philosophical reflection, sociology and psychology with research, history, environmental governance and communication, so the label captures both meaning-making and humanisation.
progression: Foundational philosophy, sociology, brain and behaviour, research methods and communication precede advanced social theory, psychology, public institutions, conflict, environmental justice and independent research. Formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Citizenship, justice & social cohesion
alternatives.concept: A Humanistic Studies direction centred on citizenship, freedom, equality, dignity and social cohesion through law, political thought, sociology, philosophy, history, rhetoric and media.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum makes rights, institutions, public reasoning, conflict and civil society its organising thread while retaining philosophical, historical and cultural reflection.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces sustained psychology, well-being, methods, sustainability and applied communication content with public, constitutional, criminal, private and EU law plus democratic institutions and historical-cultural analysis; each programme has thirteen distinct courses.
progression: Foundations in law, society, philosophy and history precede public and constitutional law, political theory, historical research, criminal and private law, EU law and advanced social theory. Formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

blocks: Matched explicitly after semantic review: Personal & Professional Development supports the first-year academic, reflective and normative-professional foundation.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Advanced Research Seminar provides a defensible UCR counterpart to the independent-research dimension of the thesis and professionalisation core.
Meaning, ethics, mind and human development
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Modern Sociology provides interdisciplinary social-theoretical deepening for analysing societal questions and modernity.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the target's 30-EC specialization, minor or study-abroad space has student-selected content and should not be assigned an invented single-course equivalent.

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the programme's broad interdisciplinary Humanistic Studies identity, while the generator-backed citizenship and social-cohesion cluster supports one coherent and materially distinct UCR direction. The remaining interests are cross-cutting content already integrated into those programmes rather than separate curricular routes; two alternatives therefore exhaust the defensible candidate set.

notes.text: UvH integrates meaning-making and humanisation across dedicated Humanistic Studies learning lines and a thesis/professional sequence. UCR can build a strong interdisciplinary analogue, but it does not award a Humanistic Studies degree or reproduce UvH's exact normative-professional identity and 30-EC specialization structure.
